sources.title: DMZ — 5 Features to Get Excited for in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s New Mode
sources.text: Call of Duty’s upcoming DMZ mode sounds like it’s shaping up to be something special. Set on the new Hajin map and inspired by the events and locations from Modern Warfare 4 ’s Campaign, this open-world combat environment will challenge you to loot, complete objectives, fight both enemies and rival Operators, and extract before everything you’ve earned is lost. Recent intel drops on the official Call of Duty Blog have given us a much clearer picture of what awaits in Hajin when DMZ launches as part of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 . Players who have digitally pre-ordered or pre-purchased Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 can gain Early Access to the game’s Campaign starting Friday, October 16 and all of DMZ starting Tuesday, October 20. The events within DMZ are set after the main MW4 Campaign, leaving a power vacuum in its wake. Now it’s up to you to identify a new, mysterious threat and dismantle its operations across the DMZ through various deployments. From scavenging for crafting materials and experimenting with new technology, to leveling up an Operator, the mode sounds like it offers plenty to look forward to. Here are five features to get excited for when you begin your deployment. The 3D Printer will be available back at the Forward Operating Base (FOB) between deployments and will serve as your primary crafting station to build equipment and upgrades for your loadout before you drop into Hajin. The Call of Duty Blog shares that , as you progress through the DMZ, you’ll unlock new crafting recipes to create more powerful equipment – as well as upgrades to the 3D Printer and even the Forward Operating Base itself. Recipes can also be found on deployments and, presuming you extract in one piece, you can then craft those items for your Operator back at the FOB. When focused on crafting new equipment, the two key things you’ll be looking for when looting on deployments will be Resources and 3D Printer Ingredients – these are the two types of main elements to craft all items. There are four basic Resources to find during a deployment: Synthetics, Electronics, Chemicals, and Metals, automatically broken down from looted items, into your Backpack and Stash. 3D Printer Ingredients are rarer materials found in specific areas of Hajin and are valuable as an ingredient to make a new Item. Examples include Binding Catalyst, Biomaterials, Detonators, and Control Units, to name a few. Once you have enough of these two types of materials, you can select how many copies of an item you want to craft at once, then choose where crafted items go: send completed items directly to your Stash for later or equip them directly to your Operator to quickly prepare for the next deployment. Having this flexibility in how you want to engage the enemy during your deployment can open a variety of experiences in DMZ and can make each deployment feel like it matters, even if you come back to the FOB with zero kills to your name – at least you’ve got handful of electronics or a comms module to make it worth your time. Extraction shooters are always more engaging when every deployment has a clear purpose. That’s not going to be problem with DMZ as it will offer three ways to deploy: Story Missions, Dynamic Operations, and Free Roam. Of those, Story Missions and Dynamic Operations are two that really stand out with their defined objectives and high-tier rewards. According to the Call of Duty Blog , Story Missions will feature narrative-led deployments that you can complete and replay, though some remain locked until prerequisites are met. Each entry provides briefing intel, required objectives, and rewards – usually high-value gear and DMZ Cash – along with options for a random mission and additional milestone rewards. Dynamic Operations, meanwhile, give squads multiple goals to pursue within the DMZ. After deploying, you choose an operation and complete its objectives to earn DMZ XP, Cash, and the ability to call in a Supply Drop filled with unpredictable loot. That extra payoff adds anticipation to every successful Op while making Dynamic Operations a promising source of both Cash and XP. Persistent Operators may be DMZ’s most exciting feature because they allow Hajin to leave a lasting mark on you. You’ll begin with two Operator slots, and unlock a third as you progress through DMZ levels. Each Operator then grows stronger by surviving deployments and earning DMZ XP. Each successful exfil levels up your Operator’s Dog Tags, and this is the key to gaining Trait Points for your Operator. You can invest those points across the Warfighter, Scout, and Survivalist Trait Trees, creating a meaningful choice between specialization and flexibility: with a maximum of 18 points to earn, and a choice of over 60 Trait Points to augment your Operator, you can tailor each Operator to your skills and preferred role. For example, Warfighter Traits include Combat Resistance, Quick Fix, and Viper Sense; Scout Traits include improved Thermal Padding, UAV Upgrade, and Field Crafting; while Survivalist Traits include Faster and Free Revives, increased Consumable Duration, and many more. But here’s where it gets dicey: if an Operator fails to extract and becomes MIA, you must either recover them with DMZ Cash or dismiss them. Because recovery costs rise with Trait investment, bringing back a high-level Operator becomes increasingly expensive. Recovered Operators keep their Traits but lose their gear, putting real weight behind every deployment. The chase for loot is at the heart of every extraction shooter, and DMZ makes each haul matter beyond the current deployment. Returning to base with a pack full of supplies doesn’t just feel rewarding – it improves your chances of success the next time you enter Hajin. Once you drop into a deployment, looting should be a top priority. Searching containers provides resources for combat, supports marked Operations, strengthens your position in Hajin, and offers a reliable way to earn DMZ XP and adva

sources.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Launch Rollout Adds DMZ Early Access
sources.text: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has added DMZ to its list of early access experiences available for pre-order players ahead of its launch later this month. Activision and Infinity Ward revealed a host of new details for its DMZ revamp in a blog post shared today. Early access for the mode joins campaign early access , with both available to those who pre-ordered either the standard or Vault Edition versions of the game across PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and/or Xbox Series X/S. Here's the full breakdown: Eligible players will gain early access to the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign starting Friday, October 16. DMZ early access will then follow Tuesday, October 20, with the full launch unleashing the rest of the experience come Friday, October 23. All of the new details arrived with a new gameplay trailer for DMZ, which you can see below. DMZ was first introduced as Call of Duty's take on the extraction shooter experience with 2022's Modern Warfare 2 . It was expanded upon in the months that followed but was ultimately deemed to be an underwhelming prototype by many. Support ended in late 2023, and now, Activision is taking another swing at it. The DMZ in Modern Warfare 4 has been propped up as a fully fleshed-out evolution for the game mode. In today's post, Infinity Ward described the new take on the mode as the series' "definitive extraction shooter experience," promising persistent progression in the open-world combat environment known as the Hajin Exclusion Zone. "There's an interesting story with the DMZ beta, where we had to make some decisions," studio multiplayer creative director Joe Cecot said in a recent behind-the-scenes video (below). "Certain things we wanted to do, we couldn't do. At the end of the day, we learned a lot: That we made a very approachable, fun sandbox that was fun to fight in, to explore, to make friends in, to get into fights in. There's a bunch of stuff we left on the table, so as soon as we finished with the last game, we were just gung-ho on, 'OK, we know what we want to do.'" Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches October 23 for PC and consoles. Our first proper look at DMZ gameplay arrived in June, with even more details shared earlier this week. While early access players will get to dive into DMZ and the story mode a few days earlier than others, core multiplayer offerings won't officially launch until that firm release date hits. You can see how the team at Infinity Ward is working to deal with wall-hack cheaters here . Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

sources.title: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls Officially Adding Thor, Venom, and Jubilee Next Year
sources.text: Arc System Works revealed three more DLC fighters coming to the game in 2027 Arc System Works and Sony Interactive Entertainment have unveiled the rest of the Year 1 DLC characters for Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls at EVO France. The first one to arrive after Phoenix Cyclops is a surprising pick. Instead of adding Thor Odinson to the tag fighter's roster, the developers chose Jane Foster's Thor. The trailer that debuted Jane Foster's Thor as a fighter also revealed the full Year 1 DLC lineup. Phoenix Cyclops kicks things off on Nov. 2. Then, in 2027, we can expect Thor (Jane Foster) to launch in the Winter, Venom in the Spring, and X-Men character Jubilee in the Summer. It's a strong group of DLC characters that come from different corners of the Marvel universe. While we didn't see any gameplay featuring Jane Foster's Thor, the trailer does show her confronting Loki in Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls ' Asgard stage. This won't be the first time Jane Foster's Thor has been playable in a video game, as she was one of Marvel's Avengers ' last post-launch characters in 2022. Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls has shown a willingness to subvert expectations with its roster picks, featuring Shuri's Black Panther rather than T'Challa's and the Phoenix Force-infused Cyclops rather than the regular version. Venom is a fairly mainstream pull, though, and he'll join the game alongside a new Klyntar stage. As a fan of X-Men: The Animated Series and X-Men '97 , I'm most hyped for Jubilee's addition. She's already a lot of fun in Marvel Rivals , and I can't wait to see how Arc System Works adapts her flashy powers for its gorgeous fighting game. Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is available on PlayStation 5 and Windows PC. To access these DLC characters, you'll need to buy the $84.99 Digital Deluxe Edition or the base game plus the $34.99 Year 1 Character and Stage Pass.

sources.text: Gears of War E-Day é bom? Confira review com o novo exclusivo do Xbox e PC O Xbox Game Pass é um dos serviços de assinatura de games mais democráticos da atualidade, já que é possível acessá-lo de diferentes plataformas — incluindo os próprios, consoles da Microsoft, assim como no PC, nuvem, celulares, tablets e até Smart TVs Samsung e LG com modelos de 2022 para cá. Felizmente, seu catálogo também é atualizado quase que semanalmente, trazendo inúmeras opções para os assinantes aproveitarem — e o melhor de tudo: gastando pouco em comparação às novas tendências de preços da indústria. Se veio em busca de novos jogos para jogar através do Xbox Game Pass , está no lugar certo. O serviço ganhou um reforço de peso esta semana com a chegada de quatro títulos para os assinantes aproveitarem. Confira abaixo mais informações sobre as novas aventuras! Gears of War: E-Day é uma prequel do primeiro jogo da franquia e acompanha Marcus Fenix e Dominic Santiago durante o Dia da Emergência, 14 anos antes dos acontecimentos originais. A campanha mostra o surgimento da Horda Locust e o início da batalha pela sobrevivência da humanidade. O game aposta na ação brutal característica da série, com uma história focada na origem dos personagens e do conflito contra os Locust. Gears of War: E-Day chegou no primeiro dia ao Xbox Game Pass. Echo Weaver é um metroidvania com foco em exploração, conhecimento e manipulação do tempo. No papel do último Tecelão, o jogador precisa aprender com cada ciclo temporal e utilizar as anomalias para encontrar uma forma de quebrar a repetição. A aventura combina exploração e resolução de mistérios, fazendo com que as informações obtidas durante as tentativas sejam parte essencial da progressão. O jogo também chegou no primeiro dia ao Xbox Game Pass. Forever Ago acompanha Alfred, que parte em uma viagem pelo norte após uma tragédia que muda sua vida. A aventura solo é centrada na exploração de diferentes lugares, no encontro com novos personagens e na busca por redenção. Durante a jornada, o jogador poderá registrar momentos com uma câmera, conhecer pessoas e construir novas amizades. Claro, Forever Ago também chegou ao Xbox Game Pass no primeiro dia. Por fim, Neon Abyss 2 combina plataforma e ação roguelike em um cenário cyberpunk repleto de elementos pixelados. Na pele de um personagem lançado em Nova Atenas, o jogador precisa enfrentar o Abismo e diferentes ameaças enquanto busca vingança. A experiência é construída em torno de tentativas sucessivas, com a morte fazendo parte da progressão. Cada derrota permite uma nova oportunidade de explorar o Abismo e avançar em meio aos desafios. stories.title: Magic: The Gathering Darkhold Destiny Panel – Everything Announced
stories.summary: Earlier this year at MagicCon in Las Vegas, Wizards of the Coast revealed its in-universe sets for 2027, but that only covered three of the six planned sets. The other three are Universes Beyond — the card game's crossover brand — and now we know about another one, Darkhold Destiny, the new Marvel set.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Magic: The Gathering Darkhold Destiny Panel – Everything Announced
sources.text: Wizards of the Coast just announced Magic: The Gathering Darkhold Destiny , its latest Marvel set in a New York Comic Con panel. This is the third Marvel collaboration for the card game, but where the first two were about presenting super heroes as they already exist in Marvel canon, Wizards of the Coast was able to cook up its own storyline for Darkhold Destiny. The set revolves around the likes of Doctor Strange, Thor and Ghost Rider, all trying to work against Hela and Dormammu invading the multiverse. It's a much better thematic fit for Magic: The Gathering, and the early cards have introduced new mechanics like Vengeance, which is like the Adventure mechanic introduced in Throne of Eldraine, but evil . Even though there was a lot of information in this panel, the set doesn't come out until April 8th next year, so there are still plenty of details that WotC is holding close to its chest. And, keep in mind that there are still two more Universes Beyond sets coming next year that we don't know anything about. 8:35 pm: And that's the show. Darkhold Destiny, looks like a cool set, but there's still a lot that Wizards didn't reveal. But it's a decent start! 8:33 pm: WotC announced a special promo or Doctor Doom, King of Latveria for Avengers Doomsday. you'll be able to grab it if you go see the movie at a Regal Cinemas on opening weekend "as long as supplies last". It's the face of the Dr. Doom commander deck, and it's done in the style of the MCU, so I expect it'll go fast. 8:31 pm: One more thing. There will be three Secret Lair drops inspired by Dr. Doom, just in time for the new Avengers movie. They're not revealing which cards are in the drop yet, but there is Dr. Doom art, and they told the crowd "you'll have to guess which reprint this is". I guess we'll wait. 8:26 pm: There are new Secret Lair, a countdown kit, a giant box with 30 cards. This thing is about to cost a lot of money. Most people will get it in nonfoil, but there will be a random chance that you'll get it in traditional foil, and an even more rare chance to get it in surge foil. I guess the Secret Lair booster packs didn't work, but we're at least getting to gamble on whether or not they're foil. The Secret Lair launches November 2nd. 8:22 pm: There will be two bundles, a regular bundle and an 'Arcanum' bundle. Both of these will have their own mechanically unique promo card. Hopefully that card doesn't get too expensive! There are also two scene boxes, also filled with mechanically unique cards. 8:19 pm: For the product suite, we have Booster Packs, Collector Boosters, Prerelease Pack and Draft Night (which also has a Collector Booster). There will also be four commander decks, Strange Academy (WUB), Gods of Asgard (RGW), Midnight Sons (WB) and Lords of Hel (BR). There will also be Collectors Editions for each deck that'll be completely decked out in surge foils. 8:16 pm: The basic lands take after the Adventures From the Forgotten Realms lands, with flavor text that tell the story. Unlike that D&D set, though, each Basic Land type has two variants, one before Hela and Dormammu's invasion and one after. They look awesome. 8:13 pm: One more card, Temple of Khonshu. It's a common black/white land and it enters tapped unless you control a Dimension. Dimension is some kind of new card type, and Wizards is not revealing it yet. I hope they're better than Battles. 8:10 pm: They brought Arcane back, which was a card subtype that hasn't really existed since the Kamigawa block in the 2000s. We got a black modal spell, and a red one "Rise From the Nether" that creates 3/1 creature tokens. Bring back Splice Onto Arcane. 8:08 pm: Hela's card looks awesome, it introduces a new keyword, Vengeance, which is basically just an Adventure that you cast when the card is in the graveyard. So, if Hela is your commander, you can send her to the graveyard when she dies, then put her in the command zone when you cast from the graveyard, and make a little loop. 8:05 pm: They introduced Magik as a dual faced card. WotC didn't add all the X-Men, but Magik fits the vibe of the set, and she looks awesome. She'll be able to transform into Darkchild, and you'll be able to pay 4 life to give her indestructible. So, she'll be pretty hard to kill. 8:03 pm: But even with all the art, there has to be cards. The centerpiece is The Darkhold, a legendary artifact for three mana, and you can tap it, put sin counters on it and draw a card for each sin counter. It's like an evil version of The One Ring. 8:01 pm: The set will be themed around three different types of magic. Arcane for Doctor Strange & Co, Divine for gods like Thor and Dark Magic for villains like Hela and Dormammu. But there are some heroes might be using Dark Magic. 7:57 pm: Once they got the greenlight, WotC had to invent a lot, apparently. The first two sets were about superheroes, but with Darkhold Destiny, the company was much more interested in focusing on villains. So, we've got Hela has a foil to Thor, and the Dread Dormammu as the foil to Doctor Strange. Hela x Dormammu is quite a cool team-up, I'm not going to lie. 7:53 pm: The main heroes of the set are Doctor Strange and Thor, which perfectly fit the theme of the set. And it's not Thor as the Avenger, it's Thor as a god. It sounds like the story really came together after Magic designers pitched their idea for a darker Marvel world. 7:52 pm: There will be new crossover comics, coming out via Infinity Comics. stories.title: GTA 6 Fan Says Rockstar Sent Them a Poster Just Because They Asked Nicely
stories.summary: A Grand Theft Auto 6 fan in Brazil said they politely asked the Rockstar Games team to send them a poster – and it looks like they actually followed through.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: GTA 6 Fan Says Rockstar Sent Them a Poster Just Because They Asked Nicely
sources.text: A Grand Theft Auto 6 fan in Brazil said they politely asked the Rockstar Games team to send them a poster – and it looks like they actually followed through. Reddit user aogustoo shared their story in a post late last month. What began as a "shot-in-the-dark email" they sent to Rockstar asking for a signed GTA 6 poster has turned into what seems to be a heartwarming moment for them and the community. "A while ago I took a complete shot in the dark and emailed Rockstar," they said. "I shared how hyped I was for GTA VI and asked if there was any chance I could get a poster for my room. "Honestly, I expected an automated reply or nothing at all. To my absolute surprise, an executive actually answered and shipped an official GTA VI poster straight from their New York office to my home in Brazil." You can see images, which show not only the poster but the emails they supposedly sent to receive it, above. As Rockstar (and the rest of the world) count down the days to GTA 6's November 19 launch, fans will no doubt be on the lookout for official merchandise like this. As many have pointed out, it's unclear if Rockstar truly took the time to send the poster, but the community is still looking to the moment as something worth celebrating as the countdown continues. "This is a massive W tho," Rockstar content creator @videotech said on X/Twitter . "This guy isn’t an influencer or someone famous, literally just a random Rockstar fan. Very kind of Rockstar and Take-Two to take the time and effort to do this." "​I blurred out all personal addresses, names, and contact emails to respect their privacy," aogustoo added. "Please don't flood their inbox with requests, as I'm pretty sure this was just a rare act of kindness from someone on their team." There's still so much about GTA 6 that we don’t know, but one thing is for sure: Rockstar will probably get even more emails after this. While we wait to learn more about the next Grand Theft Auto game ahead of its November 19 launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, you can check out IGN's recent interview with Rockstar North's Rob Nelson . You can also read about what Nintendo had to say about the chances of seeing GTA 6 on Switch 2 , some recently revealed radio stations , and even a batch of new screenshots . stories.title: Star Citizen Single-Player Spinoff Squadron 42 Reemerges With Flashy New Trailer, Steam Wishlists, and Cast Confirmation
stories.summary: Star Citizen developer Cloud Imperium Games has pulled back the curtain on single-player spinoff Squadron 42 with a new cinematic trailer, the launch of Steam wishlists, and a full cast reveal.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Star Citizen Single-Player Spinoff Squadron 42 Reemerges With Flashy New Trailer, Steam Wishlists, and Cast Confirmation
sources.text: Star Citizen developer Cloud Imperium Games has pulled back the curtain on single-player spinoff Squadron 42 with a new cinematic trailer, the launch of Steam wishlists, and a full cast reveal. Squadron 42 is the story-driven off-shoot of space sim Star Citizen, which Cloud Imperium Games has worked on for the last 12 years. Its 12-year development is led by Chris Roberts, creator of the Wing Commander series. Indeed, Squadron 42 is a spiritual successor to Wing Commander, and like the Wing Commander games, Squadron 42 features a string of Hollywood stars, such as Mark Hamill, Gary Oldman, Gillian Anderson, Ben Mendelsohn, and Henry Cavill. The game fuses space combat, first-person shooter action, and a character-driven narrative supported by full performance capture. CIG said the performances are woven directly into gameplay, so you won’t just see those famous actors within cinematics. And here’s what to expect from the structure of the game: The trailer shows a decent amount of gameplay, including first-person sections, some of which involve platforming and puzzle solving, ship customization, off duty activities, a hacking mini-game, and a glimpse at narrative choices. Ian Duncan, best known for playing Todd Todmore on BBC comedy Broken News, is the male player character, and prolific video game actor Alix Wilton Regan (Samantha Traynor in Mass Effect 3, the female Inquisitor in Dragon Age: Inquisition, Aya in Assassin's Creed Origins, and Lara Croft in the upcoming Tomb Raider games) plays the female player character. In August, CIG delayed Squadron 42 to Q2 2027 , with Roberts insisting it wouldn’t get the attention it deserves if it came out at the end of 2026 because of November’s GTA 6. "At CitizenCon 2024, we announced we would ship in 2026. Our plan was to release in Q4 around IAE," Roberts said at the time. "But much like the rest of the industry there is no way I want to launch my spiritual successor to Wing Commander, a game that has had 12 years of blood, sweat and tears invested into it (we started Squadron 42 development in 2014 as 2013 was opening studios, hiring people and getting the Hangar module out for Star Citizen) launching into the attention buzz saw of GTA 6. While GTA 6 isn’t launching on PC this November, pretty much all outlets and most content creators will be all over it, not leaving a lot of room for other coverage." The delay announcement came hot on the heels of a disastrous Star Citizen developer livestream that went radically off the rails . After early access players complained of bugs and issues with a new update to the game, CIG held a stream to show the "intended" version of the experience, only to be met with the same issues, if not worse. It led to passive-aggressive comments between the developers themselves and an uncomfortable tension in the air. Star Citizen crossed the $1 billion raised barrier in May — a significant milestone that came shortly after a $5,000 virtual spaceship you couldn’t actually fly in-game went on sale. It’s since raised a further $50 million. Star Citizen is considered one of the most controversial projects in all video games. Over the 14 years since its crowdfunding drive began, Star Citizen has been called many things, including a scam by those who wonder whether it will ever properly launch. Its virtual ships, some of which cost thousands of dollars, are often the focus of criticism. But its loyal fanbase insist it's one of the most compelling space sims around, and continue to pump millions of dollars into the project via ship sales. Star Citizen itself remains without a release window. Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

sources.title: Squadron 42 has a Steam page
sources.text: Star Citizen's singleplayer mode gets a new trailer and more signs of life. In August, game director Chris Roberts said that Star Citizen's singleplayer component, Squadron 42, was being delayed out of 2026 to avoid clashing with Grand Theft Auto 6 . There was a certain amount of skepticism about the reason for the delay, thanks in part to a recent Star Citizen livestream being declared a disaster , but also because, well. These games have had so many release dates the changes have their own wiki page . There's something concrete about having Squadron 42 getting a Steam page though, with system requirements and everything. Those system requirements are charmingly old-fashioned, with no mention of ray tracing-capable GPUs or DirectX 12. Although the install size of 150GB is still pretty hefty. ( Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is apparently going to be 200GB , oof.) There's also a new trailer, which leans heavily on the oorah stuff that's always a bit of a turn-off in military science-fiction. Privateer was my favorite Wing Commander game because it left out all the Top Gun nonsense, but of course it's front-and-center in Squadron 42. So too are the celebrity actors, with appearances by Mark Hamill, Gary Oldman, Rhona Mitra, that guy who played the Onion Knight in Game of Thrones, and other people who probably filmed most of their scenes a solid decade ago now. We also get to see a fair bit of the male version of the player-character, who will doubtless BroShep his way into most of the promos even though I'll be picking the one voiced by Alix Wilton Regan instead. The Steam page lists Squadron 42's release date as Q2 2027, and I'd love to see it actually release on that date and be the solid combo of Wing Commander and Half-Life 2 that happens to have Gillian Anderson and Henry Cavill in the cutscenes that's being promised here. It could happen.
